# Zero Slop

Zero Slop is an open-source AI writing humanizer and anti-slop checker. It scores the recognizable AI accent in prose and identifies the phrases and structural patterns behind it. It then rewrites the draft and verifies that facts were not dropped or invented.

## Core facts

- Website: https://zero-slop.ai/
- Full product reference: https://zero-slop.ai/llms-full.txt
- Source and documentation: https://github.com/manavmishra/ZeroSlop
- Latest release: https://github.com/manavmishra/ZeroSlop/releases/latest
- License: MIT
- Price: Free
- Runtime: Standard-library Python scorer; no third-party packages required
- Privacy: The scorer runs offline and requires no account or server
- Supported environments: Agents that support SKILL.md files, including Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Warp, and Zed

## Install

`npx skills add manavmishra/ZeroSlop --global`

## What makes it different

Zero Slop is not an authorship detector. It is an editorial tool that measures known tell phrases, sentence rhythm, readability, and formatting. After two rewrite passes, Zero Slop scores the result, runs a read-aloud check, and compares that version with the original before returning the finished draft.

## Examples on the website

The website includes before-and-after sample rewrites for a LinkedIn post, blog introduction, strategy document, X thread, and PowerPoint slide. The displayed likelihood scores come from the open-source Zero Slop scorer, and lower scores indicate fewer AI-like writing patterns.
